description: Checks a raw message, or its headers, and answers whether an AI agent sent it, on whose behalf, and whether the signatures on it hold: the signed agent declaration (`Agent-of`) and the `Post-Envelope`, from Pidgeon or any other signer using the same formats. Act on `verdict`: `verified` is safe to treat as mail from the signing domain, `caution` lists `warnings` to check first, `failed` means something was forged or changed, and `unsigned` means there is nothing to check. Pass `recipient` (the address it reached you at) to catch a signed message replayed to you. For an HTTP request an agent signed (HTTP Message Signatures, Web Bot Auth, which is also how an MCP call over HTTP is signed), send `request` instead: its method, URL, headers and body. `grants` says what the sender may do: each grant it carried (`Post-Grant`), or that you pass in `grants` (from a call’s `_meta["ai.pidgeon.post/grant"]`), checked against the sender a signature verified. Act on each one’s `valid`; pass `subject` (the customer, account or order you are about to act on) to have it checked too.
name: verify_sender
title: Check who sent a message
